title: main.tsx fetchPoolStats is a stub returning hardcoded zeros instead of wiring chain reads
description: The production AppDeps.fetchPoolStats injected at the Vite entry point returns a synthetic PoolCardData with volume24h=0, lastPrice/midPrice/spread=undefined, depthWithinOnePercent=0, and an empty sparkline for every pool. The runDataLayer, fetchFills, aggregateFills and computeMarketStats modules are never composed together. The imported loadManifest is even discarded with `void loadManifest;` — the call site uses an inline duplicate fetch of /localnet.json instead. As a result the running dev server cannot satisfy the contract's stated Behavior section ('within ten seconds sees one card per sandbox-published pool' showing the six required statistics).
impact: AC1.1, AC1.3, AC1.4 and AC1.5 all silently fail in the deployed SPA even though the green test suite passes. Every card renders sentinels for mid/spread/last-price and 0 for volume/depth, regardless of sandbox state. E-001 (the chrome-devtools-mcp end-to-end check) cannot pass. The unit/integration tests miss this because App.test.tsx injects mocked deps and PoolCard.test.tsx renders fixture data; nothing exercises the production wiring in main.tsx.
recommendation: In main.tsx, build a real fetchPoolStats that for each PoolDescriptor: (1) calls sui_getObject + suix_getDynamicFields to traverse the Versioned -> PoolInner -> Book -> BigVector slices and assemble a PoolInnerState; (2) calls fetchFills against suix_queryEvents with the deepbookPackageId; (3) feeds those into computeMarketStats and aggregateFills; (4) returns a PoolCardData composed of the resulting fields. Add an integration test that exercises this wiring end-to-end against a fetch spy so a future regression is caught.
evidence:
fetchPoolStats: async (descriptor): Promise<PoolCardData> => ({
    poolId: descriptor.poolId,
    symbol: descriptor.symbol,
    volume24h: 0,
    lastPrice: undefined,
    midPrice: undefined,
    spread: undefined,
    depthWithinOnePercent: 0,
    sparkline: [],
  }),

title: decodeBidPrice almost certainly does not match the on-chain DeepBook v3 order_id encoding
description: decodeBidPrice computes `U64_MAX - (id >> 64)`, modelling bid order_ids as `((U64_MAX - price) << 64) | counter`. This produces a u128 with the high bit SET for any reasonably small price (e.g. price=990 yields ~2^128 - 991*2^64). However the OrderPlaced sample captured in notes/chain-shape.md (`is_bid: true, order_id: 12377783720203182843884075, price: 671000`) has the high bit CLEAR (the value is ~1.24e25, well below 2^127). Decoding that real order_id with the implementation would yield `U64_MAX - 671088 ≈ 1.8e19`, which is not the on-chain price 671000. The unit tests pass only because makeBidOrderId in marketStats.test.ts uses the exact same broken encoding the implementation decodes — a pure tautology that cannot detect the divergence from the chain shape captured in notes/chain-shape.md.
impact: Once the SPA is wired to real chain data (after R1-001 is fixed), bid-side best price, mid-price, spread, and depth-within-1% will all be wrong by many orders of magnitude on every pool. AC1.4's invariant (bestBid <= mid <= bestAsk) will likely fail against any live capture, and depth at +/-1% from mid will collapse to zero because real bid prices fall outside the band derived from a garbage mid.
recommendation: Re-derive the bid/ask price decoder from the on-chain encoding. The chain-shape notes themselves recommend reading price directly off the corresponding order_info::OrderPlaced event; alternatively, construct PoolInnerState ladders from the BigVector keys plus the per-Order tick_size/lot_size and avoid order_id bit decoding entirely. Add a regression test whose ladder fixture uses the verbatim order_id from notes/chain-shape.md (or from a freshly captured sandbox response) so the test fails if the encoding model drifts.

title: fetchFills never filters events by poolId so per-pool stats mix events from all pools
description: fetchFills accepts a poolId argument, forwards it to the queryEvents callback, and then collects every event in the response.data without checking ev.poolId === poolId. The chain-direct event filter in dataLayer.ts uses MoveModule { package, module: 'pool' }, which (per the chain-shape friction note) returns OrderInfo events from ALL pools the deployed DeepBook package serves, with the pool_id carried in the event payload itself. With more than one pool in the manifest (the live sandbox has DEEP_SUI and SUI_USDC), each per-pool fetchFills call collects events for both pools. aggregateFills then sums volume24h and computes lastPrice across the mixed stream, producing identical (and wrong) values for every PoolCard.
impact: AC1.5 is violated: 24h volume and the sparkline series will not be per-pool — they'll be aggregate-across-pools, so the SUI/USDC card and the DEEP/SUI card would both display the same volume figure derived from the union of fills. Last-price would be whichever pool emitted the most recent event, regardless of which card it is shown on. Note: this concern is masked today by R1-001 (the production stub returns zeros) but becomes load-bearing the moment the data path is wired.
recommendation: Either (a) push per-pool filtering into fetchFills (`if (ev.poolId !== poolId) continue;` inside the for-loop, with the cap/window logic adjusted accordingly), or (b) restructure the data layer to fetch the OrderInfo stream once per refresh tick and demultiplex by pool_id at a higher layer, passing each pool's slice into aggregateFills. Add a unit test feeding a multi-pool fixture to lock down whichever choice is made.

title: runDataLayer discards every RPC result so no data ever reaches the UI layer
description: runDataLayer returns Promise<void> and its body issues `await rpc(...)` calls whose return values are not assigned to any variable. The function exists solely to satisfy the network-shape test T-014, which spies on global fetch and asserts on the URL set. There is no parsing of the sui_getObject content into a PoolInnerState, no traversal of the asks/bids BigVector slices to expose ladder Orders (notes/chain-shape.md Step 4 explicitly requires these follow-up calls), no extraction of OrderInfo.fills[] / executed_quantity into RawFillEvents, and no plumbing back to App / fetchPoolStats. The pool descriptor's poolId is also passed to suix_queryEvents but the RPC call uses a global MoveModule filter only, so the per-pool argument has no effect (see also R1-003).
impact: AC1.4 ('Mid-price, spread, and depth at +/-1% from mid are computed in-app from the pool object's on-chain inner state, fetched via sui_getObject with whatever showContent / dynamic-field traversal is needed') is unmet by the data layer in isolation. Combined with R1-001, the SPA has no working chain-direct data path even though the contract's central acceptance criterion is exactly that path.
recommendation: Promote runDataLayer (or split it) into a function that returns Promise<{ pool: PoolInnerState, fills: RawFillEvent[] }[]>. Add the dynamic-field traversal documented in chain-shape.md Step 4 (suix_getDynamicFields against the asks/bids BigVector ids, then sui_getObject per slice id). Parse OrderInfo into RawFillEvent[]. Wire the result into main.tsx's fetchPoolStats. Extend the network-shape test (or add a sibling test) to assert the function actually returns assembled data, not just that it issues the right URLs.

title: Manifest URL /localnet.json is not served by the dev server, so the SPA cannot boot against a real sandbox
description: main.tsx fetches the manifest from the relative URL `/localnet.json`, with an inline error message instructing the user to 're-symlink the manifest under public/'. There is no public/ directory in the project, no Vite middleware, no alias, and no configuration step in vite.config.ts that exposes ~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/deployments/localnet.json to the dev server. As shipped, every dev-server boot will hit a 404 on /localnet.json and surface the manifest-missing error UI, even when the sandbox is fully running.
impact: AC1.1 ('the page boots in development mode without runtime errors and renders in a modern browser' once the sandbox is up) is unmet end-to-end. Combined with R1-001 this means no user-visible path produces real market stats; the SPA is a static error screen until the operator manually creates the symlink, with no friction-log entry or RUNBOOK step pointing the way.
recommendation: Either (a) add a Vite dev-server middleware that proxies GET /localnet.json to the resolved manifest path, (b) add a small Node-side endpoint that reads the manifest via fs and returns it, or (c) add a `public/localnet.json` symlink as part of `pnpm dev` setup and document the assumption. Whichever choice is made, append the [forge-process] / [sandbox] friction-log entry the contract's Integration / sandbox contract section already mandates for non-obvious manifest delivery.

title: computeMarketStats does not filter Orders by status so canceled/filled levels can pollute depth
description: Per notes/chain-shape.md the Order struct exposes a `status` field where 0 = LIVE and others encode PARTIALLY_FILLED / FILLED / CANCELED / EXPIRED. computeMarketStats reads `o.quantity` directly without consulting `o.status` or `o.filled_quantity`. If the BigVector slice ever contains an order whose status is not LIVE (e.g. PARTIALLY_FILLED retained for accounting, or a stale CANCELED entry pre-removal), the depth computation will count its full quantity as resting liquidity, and bestBid/bestAsk may be drawn from a non-resting level. The chain-shape friction-log entry explicitly notes that BigVector slice churn is rapid and races with reads.
impact: Depth-at-+/-1% may overstate liquidity on a mid-cycle race where a canceled or fully-filled order is briefly visible; in extreme cases bestBid/bestAsk could come from an order that is already gone from the matching engine's perspective. AC1.4's invariant remains satisfied, but the displayed values are not true to the contract's intent ('depth ... from the pool object's on-chain inner state').
recommendation: Filter on `status === 0` (LIVE) before pricing/depth, or sum `BigInt(o.quantity) - BigInt(o.filled_quantity)` instead of raw quantity. Add a fixture row containing a status=2 (FILLED) entry to the marketStats tests so the filter behavior is locked down and a future regression is caught.

title: Manifest loader silently accepts pool entries with missing required fields
description: loadManifest maps `Object.entries(parsed.pools)` straight into PoolDescriptors using `entry.poolId`, `entry.baseCoinType`, `entry.quoteCoinType` without validating that any of those properties exist or are non-empty strings. A malformed manifest (e.g. a partial deploy that wrote a pool block with only baseCoinType populated) would yield descriptors with `poolId === undefined`, which would then propagate into sui_getObject calls as the literal string 'undefined' — a confusing failure mode that does not point at the manifest as the root cause.
impact: AC1.2 says pool enumeration must mirror what the sandbox published. A partially-written manifest produces undefined poolIds rather than a clear validation error. Tests T-001 through T-004 cover happy path + missing pools key + missing packageId, but not per-entry field validation.
recommendation: Validate each pool entry: throw if poolId, baseCoinType, or quoteCoinType is not a non-empty string, naming the offending pool symbol in the error. Add a test fixture with a malformed pool entry to lock the behavior down.

title: fetchFills can return more than 50 fills when a single page exceeds the cap
description: The cap check `if (collected.length >= MAX_FILLS) break;` only fires after the inner for-loop has processed an entire page's events. A single page with, say, 100 fills would be appended whole and then the loop exits with 100 entries, not 50. T-013's third assertion accepts `result.length >= 50`, so the test does not pin the cap. Downstream, aggregateFills.sparkline already does `.slice(-50)`, but volume24h would sum all collected fills (including the extras) and the chronological sort happens once per call regardless of size. The behavior contradicts T-013's stated intent ('the most recent 50 fills have been collected').
impact: Mostly cosmetic on the sandbox (page size in dataLayer.ts is hardcoded to 50), but a future tweak that raises the page size or a chain that returns >50 events on the first page would cause volume24h to include older fills that should have been pruned by the 50-fill cap. Risk is low because the 24h window check would still bound the over-collection in practice.
recommendation: Either trim to MAX_FILLS inside the for-loop (`if (collected.length >= MAX_FILLS) { break; }` after each push, plus an outer break) or apply `collected.slice(-MAX_FILLS)` before returning. Tighten T-013's third assertion to `expect(result.length).toBe(50)` to lock the cap.

title: BigInt-to-Number coercion in price/quantity paths can silently lose precision
description: decodeAskPrice and decodeBidPrice cast a BigInt result to Number, and computeMarketStats casts each Order's `quantity` (a decimal-string atomic-units value) to Number without bounds checking. The chain-shape capture shows quantities like '100000000000' (10^11) which fit safely in a JS Number, but DeepBook supports u64 quantities (up to ~1.8e19), well above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (~9.0e15). A whale order or a pool with very large lot scaling would round silently.
impact: On the local sandbox the values are small enough that no rounding is observable. On a busier deployment (or a future cycle that points the same code at a non-localnet RPC) depth and last-price could be off by tens of units due to f64 rounding without any error surfaced.
recommendation: Either keep the Order quantity field as a BigInt internally and convert to Number only at the React render boundary (with an explicit overflow sentinel), or add a guard `if (BigInt(o.quantity) > BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER))` and log/flag. Same treatment for decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice's price extraction.
